8387594: AArch64: Support vector integer division for SVE

Lane-wise integer division divides each vector lane independently. It is
produced both by the Vector API (Byte/Short/Int/LongVector.div(...) and
lanewise(VectorOperators.DIV, ...), masked and unmasked) and by C2
auto-vectorization of scalar loops such as `a[i] = b[i] / c`.

Currently, the AArch64 backend only supports lane-wise division of
floating-point types, there is no support for integer types today. So
the Vector API executes it through the Java fallback (a scalar loop
under VectorSupport.binaryOp), which is slow. The reasons are:
- NEON has no integer vector divide instruction at all.
- SVE provides `SDIV`, but only for 32-bit (S) and 64-bit (D) element
  sizes; there is no 8-bit or 16-bit integer divide.

This change implements lane-wise integer vector division on the SVE
backend for all integer element types:
- INT / LONG: emitted directly with SVE `SDIV`.
- SHORT: no native 16-bit divide, so each lane is sign-extended to
  32-bit, divided with `SDIV`, and narrowed back (2x `SDIV`).
- BYTE: widened to SHORT and reuses the SHORT path (4x SDIV), then
  narrowed back to BYTE.
- Masked: INT/LONG use the predicated `SDIV`; BYTE/SHORT are lowered to
  an unpredicated divide combined with `VectorBlend`.

The operations are SVE-only; on NEON-only machines they keep falling
back to scalar code.

Divide-by-zero / inactive lanes are safe because the VectorAPI checks
for these situations in the Java layer. Auto-vectorization only occurs
when the divisor is not zero, and it does not generate masked lanewise
`DIV` operations.

Replacing the Java scalar fallback with SVE `SDIV` gives a large speedup
for lane-wise integer division. And we also observed significant uplifts
for relative auto-vectorization cases.The VectorAPI JMH benchmarks are
in the panama-vector/vectorIntrinsics branch [1].
